court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: Commissioner of Police Greater Chennai Corporation and Others … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Petitioner(s): M/s. T.R. Ravi R.P. Rajkumar Alagesh
For Respondent(s): Mr. Leonard Arul Joseph Selvam, Additional Public Prosecutor, For R 1 And R 2
judgment_text:
ORDER

1. This Criminal Original Petition has been filed seeking a direction to the second respondent Police not to harass the petitioner based on the complaint given by the third respondent.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that he is running a pawn broker and jewllery shop. The petitioner had received certain gold jewels from his co-brother, Chandra Prakash, which originally belonged to one Praveen Hincot. Subsequently, the petitioner returned the gold jewels to Chandra Prakash, who in turn handed over the same to the said Praveen Hincot. It is further stated that the said Chandra Prakash had independent business, as he suffered heavy losses, he committed suicide. The said Praveen Hincot, who is the father-in-law of the third respondent, also died a natural death. Taking advantage of the above circumstances, the present complaint has been lodged seeking return of the gold jewels.

3. The petitioner would further state that he had appeared before the respondent on 16-2-2026 and gave his Explanation. However, the third respondent is making unnecessary claim without any material, which the second respondent is also supporting. Hence, the present petition.

4. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondents 1 and 2 submitted that the third respondent has lodged a complaint to the Commissioner of Police and the same was forwarded to the second respondent in C. No. 52/DCB/2025. The petitioner had appeared before the second respondent and gave his Explanation and had also agreed to resolve the issue. However, thereafter, the petitioner did not respond and has filed the present petition.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner on instructions submitted that the petitioner will appear before the second respondent on 17-3-2026 and give his Explanation.

6. In view of the above submissions, the petitioner is directed to appear before the second respondent on 17-3-2026 and give his Explanation. It is made clear that the second respondent Police shall not unnecessarily harass the petitioner or compel him to settle the claim in the absence of any material. If any material is available, appropriate action shall be taken against the petitioner in accordance with law.

7. With the above directions, the Criminal Original Petition is disposed of.
